newsitem.title: FRANCE: French chemists probed over deadly growth hormones.
newsitem.headline: French chemists probed over deadly growth hormones.

text.p: A French magistrate is probing two former health officials on suspicion that they knowingly distributed tainted growth hormones blamed for killing 40 children judicial sources said on Wednesday.

Henri Cerceau, the ex-director of the Central Pharmacy of state-run hospitals, and Marc Mollet, its former scientific director, were formally placed under investigation for possible poisoning over the distribution of about 20,000 doses of the hormones.
Magistrate Marie-Odile Bertella-Geffroy is already probing four other people for manslaughter in the case, in which children suffering from dwarfism were treated with tainted hormones from 1984-86.
"Poisoning" is a more serious charge than manslaughter and can bring a 30-year jail sentence.
The hormone, extracted from the pituitary glands of corpses, was banned from June 1985.

Investigators suspect that old stocks of the hormone were used up after the ban to save money even though officials were aware they risked causing the incurable brain-wasting Creutzfeldt-Jakob (CJD) disease.
A variant of CJD is the human equivalent of mad cow disease.
About 50 children treated with the hormone from 1984-86 contracted CJD, and 40 of them have since died, lawyers for their relatives say.

"In the whole world there are only 90 victims and 50 French people among them. The action of the French health authorities in this matter has been disastrous," said lawyer Monique Pelletier. "This is a sad record held by France."
The state-run Central Hospital Pharmacy distributes medicines to hospitals.
The case has similarities to the distribution of AIDS-tainted blood products in France in the 1980s. More than 1,250 haemophiliacs were infected and more than 400 have since died.
